title: Partial-Quasi-Newton Methods: Efficient Algorithms for Minimax Optimization Problems with Unbalanced Dimensionality

problem.claim: Strongly-convex-strongly-concave minimax optimization problems with unbalanced dimensionality.

gap.claim: Conventional minimax optimization algorithms focus on reducing total oracle calls while ignoring the unbalanced computational costs of accessing information from the two variables.

contributions.claim: A second-order Partial-Quasi-Newton method that exploits unbalanced problem structure to establish Hessian estimates efficiently.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the Partial-Quasi-Newton method as a novel second-order optimization algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors theoretically prove that PQN converges to the saddle point faster than existing minimax optimization algorithms.
Numerical experiments on real-world applications report that PQN performs significantly better than state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies strongly-convex-strongly-concave minimax optimization with unbalanced dimensionality.
The problem setting includes applications such as few-shot learning and fairness-aware machine learning.
Conventional iterative algorithms overlook unequal computational costs between the two minimax variables.
The authors propose PQN, which uses the unbalanced structure to estimate the Hessian efficiently.
The authors report faster theoretical convergence and better numerical performance than existing methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies unequal information-access costs for the two minimax variables as a limitation of conventional algorithms.

interpretation.claim: Algorithm design may benefit from accounting for asymmetric computational costs rather than optimizing only aggregate oracle-call counts.

application.claim: When designing minimax optimizers, consider partial or asymmetric second-order updates tailored to variable-specific access costs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the reported advantages hold beyond the strongly-convex-strongly-concave setting with unbalanced dimensionality.

unknowns: Specific convergence rate and assumptions are not provided.
The dimensions, computational-cost model, and Hessian-estimation details are not provided.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
